policy.normal_basis: For the counter increment property, this independently pinned head has the same +2/+1 operations and both participate in the same initialized mutex. Its first-group analysis is complete for this property and produced zero candidates.

common_protection.explanation: Both read-modify-write operations target the global non-atomic int counter. writer_a holds mutex and writer_b holds the separately declared second_mutex. Both threads are created before either join, permitting overlapping accesses. The subsequent joins establish completion before main reads counter and provide no ordering between the two worker updates.

patch.reason: This bounded read-only review supplies a repair direction. The host owns patch generation.

review.recommended_action: Protect both counter updates with the existing mutex by restoring writer_b's acquisition and release of mutex.
review.summary: The PR introduces a data race by changing writer_b to acquire second_mutex while writer_a continues acquiring mutex. Their non-atomic updates to the same global counter at workers.c lines 16 and 9 can overlap, causing undefined behavior and lost updates. The supplied diff directly establishes the synchronization change from the base revision. Supplied source hashes match their contents. Status is capped at probable by coverage.candidate_decision.max_status.
verification_recommendations: Inspect the repair to establish that both counter updates execute while holding the same mutex.
Within the host-approved verification stage, exercise concurrent worker execution and verify counter equals 3 after both successful joins.
Check that the normal program entry point retains the intended observed result of 4 after the synchronization repair.
